capabilities: Create memory cards from Markdown notes with trace links back to the source passage
Study decks with FSRS6 scheduling, Q&A, cloze, fill-in, and multiple-choice questions
Run document quizzes and exam question banks with mastery analytics
Import CSV and APKG, and back up or restore card data in the vault
Expose a public API (getOfficialAPI) for third-party plugins to create and manage cards
extras: Freemium: core loop is free, Premium is a one-time purchase unlocking advanced analytics, management views, exam banks, and AI card creation. Part of a three-plugin Weave series; requires Obsidian 1.7.0+; warns against bulk-renaming .wdeck/.qbank files.
motivation: The author wants review and notes to be one world: cards come from files, stay linked to files, and let you jump back to the source passage for context.
problem: Reviewing cards is usually disconnected from note-taking: Anki-style tools live in separate apps with field forms, and cards lose their link to the note text they came from.

relations.evidence: Traditional Anki approach | Weave Deck approach
EPUB Reader adds in-book excerpts and book-anchor jumps
Incremental Reading handles reading queues and scheduling

summary: Spaced-repetition flashcard plugin that makes Markdown memory cards linked to their source notes, with FSRS6 review, decks, quizzes, and APKG import.
